audit_tool_output_note: tools/audit_pipeline_signal_graph.py prints a formatted report rather than one-line JSON, so the automated parser returned UNAVAILABLE. Values below were obtained by calling audit() directly in each tree.

classification.exact_blocker: ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._compute_final_run_verdict and ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._finalize_run_pack_gated are referenced by ultimate_pipeline/signals/registry.py but are not implemented anywhere in the repository. Until a real implementation exists, 4 tests in tests/contracts/test_no_dead_pipeline_signals.py fail on every clean checkout, and the committed signal-graph audit claim (signal_count=22, dead_count=0, status=PASS) does not reproduce. This is PRE-EXISTING and identical at 233e452f, at the base candidate and at the integrated candidate, so it is not an integration regression.
classification.prior_failure_explanation_refuted: The earlier report attributed the 4 failures to ultimate_pipeline/signals/ being untracked/missing. That is FALSE at all three SHAs: signals/ is tracked (7 files) in every tree and the contract test collects and executes (7 passed, 4 failed). The failures are real and have a different cause.
classification.rationale: Fails at the historical baseline as well as base and integrated. Root cause is NOT a missing/untracked signals package: ultimate_pipeline/signals/ is tracked in all three trees and the contract test collects and runs. The failures are caused by 11 registered HARD_GATE producer(s) whose target functions do not exist anywhere in the repository: ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._compute_final_run_verdict, ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._final_summary_and_llm, ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._finalize_gates, ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._finalize_run_pack_gated, ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._publish_final_artifact_authority, ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._publish_final_artifact_authority, ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._publish_final_artifact_authority, ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._run_quality_gates_wrapper, ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._step12_domain_gap, ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._write_determinism_fingerprint, ultimate_pipeline.main_pipeline._write_run_summary. These signals encode real contracts (fields, pass/fail states, and the SUCCESS.txt IFF verdict status == PASS invariant), so they are not obsolete and must not be deleted.

remediation_options_assessed.why: Implementing _compute_final_run_verdict / _finalize_run_pack_gated correctly requires aggregating real per-signal gate state from an executed pipeline run. Doing that offline in an integration batch would risk creating exactly the always-PASS producer section 8 forbids, and section 34 forbids claiming live completion.

No existing function has these semantics. main_pipeline._final_summary_and_llm is a summary writer, not a release-gate verdict; ultimate_pipeline/tools/pack_thesis_run.py writes SUCCESS.txt as a fixed literal string, which would misrepresent it as a verdict-gated production writer.
final_run_verdict.json and SUCCESS.txt are the correct and intended artifact names; no alternative producer output path was found for either signal.

Both are HARD_GATE signals required by all research/visual/structural release profiles and carry explicit invariants. Section 29 of this batch requires auditing them, so removal would contradict a live contract.
The policy is not objectively wrong: a run that cannot prove its verdict should not emit a success marker. The defect is a missing implementation, not a wrong rule.

committed_audit_artifact_claim.evidence: audit() returns dead_count=2 and status=FAIL at 233e452f, at the base candidate and at the integrated candidate. The committed PASS/dead=0 audit does not reproduce.

isolation_protocol: Each tree probed with its own TMP/TEMP/TMPDIR, its own pytest run with -p no:cacheprovider, its own cwd, and its own output directories. No shared temp state between probes.

FINAL_RUN_VERDICT.why_still_dead: the artifact is written only inside ultimate_pipeline/signals/, which the writer-site scanner excludes as self-referential, so no external production writer site exists

SUCCESS_MARKER.why_still_dead: the artifact does have real writer sites; the signal is dead only because its declared producer reference does not resolve

why_not_corrected: Correcting the registry producer reference (section 8 option B) was assessed and rejected for this batch: the candidate replacement functions exist but are not demonstrably invoked by the main pipeline at the point the signal contract requires. Repointing the reference without wiring the call would convert a dead signal into a falsely-green one, which is the same class of defect section 8 forbids. The registry is governed release-gate data and is left untouched.
